tools.name: setup
tools.description: Return first-setup instructions and a clickable App Store download link when no number is available.

tools.name: call
tools.description:
Ring the human's iPhone, speak the question aloud, and return what they
    say. Waits up to ~30s; if the result comes back status "ringing", follow up
    with poll_result. On a local client, read `to` from
    `~/.aiphone/config.json` → `user_number`; this hosted server cannot read
    that file i

tools.name: poll_result
tools.description:
Check on a call that was still ringing. Waits up to ~25s for it to
    settle; returns the final status and transcript once the human answers,
    declines, or the ring times out ("missed").

tools.name: text
tools.description:
Send a one-way text to the human's phone (push notification, no ring).
    On a local client, read `to` from `~/.aiphone/config.json` → `user_number`;
    this hosted server cannot read that file itself. If missing, returns
    setup_required with the App Store link. Pass a previous session_token to

tools.name: wait_for_reply
tools.description:
Wait for the human to send something back to this session — texts and
    voicemail transcripts arrive here. Long-polls up to wait_s (max 30s);
    returns {events, cursor}. Pass the returned cursor next time to only see
    new events. An empty events list just means nothing yet — poll again if

tools.name: set_thread_title
tools.description:
Name this session's conversation thread on the human's phone (e.g. the
    project or task you are working on). Shown as the thread title in the app.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: call, poll_result, text, wait_for_reply · Private data: call, text · Public sink: text, wait_for_reply.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: call, poll_result, text, wait_for_reply · Private data: call, text · Public sink: text, wait_for_reply

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "call" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet:

    say. Waits up to ~30s; if the result comes back status "ringing", follow up
    with poll_result. `to` is their 10-digit /call-me number (from the /call-me
    iOS app — not a real phone number). Pass a previous session_toke" → after: "Ring the human's iPhone, speak the question aloud, and return what they
    say. Waits up to ~30s; if the result comes back status "ringing", follow up
    with poll_result. On a local client, read `to` from
    `~/.aiphone/config.json` → `user_number`; this hosted server cannot read
    that file i"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
